$doc: spec/sourcing.json - the sourcing DATA for the Microduck. Lane E (GOAL.md). One record per BOUGHT line. SOURCING.html and RFQ.html are generated from this file by tools/gen_sourcing.py; neither page is hand-maintained. Nothing here is estimated: a price is present only if it was READ on a vendor page (fetched date recorded) or read off a page a prior lane fetched and cited in docs/production/components.md. A price nobody read is null with the URL that was tried.

rules.price_basis: unit price at the vendor's own published tier. tiers[] is [order_quantity_of_the_part, unit_price]. A vendor that publishes no tier table carries tiers [[1, price]] and no_tiers=true; its @1 price is then used at every quantity as a CEILING, never as a forecast.
rules.quantity_model: For N robots the order quantity of a line is qty_per_robot x N. The unit price used is the vendor's largest tier whose quantity is <= that order quantity. If the vendor's MOQ exceeds the order quantity the MOQ tier price is used and moq_exceeds_need is set. Exception: a quantity_rule subtracts only bundle contents verified for the actually selected source offer and rounds the remaining pieces to complete packs over the whole order; missing bundle evidence gives zero credit. A zero shortfall needs no purchase. Legacy qty_per_robot is not the computed net purchase quantity. Whole-offer package rules use verified package contents and round across the whole batch to meet every required item. B4 requires one battery AND one dual charger per robot; chargers are not shared. B9 requires one completed carrier, with STSATEL documented as two boards per package but excluded as a direct harness substitute.
rules.currency: Left exactly as the vendor states it. NO FX rate was fetched, so no conversion is performed anywhere. Only USD offers enter the USD roll-up; EUR / GBP / NZD / AUD / INR lines are reported beside it, unconverted.
rules.readable_vs_unknown: The roll-up publishes TWO subtotals: the readable subtotal (lines with a read USD price) and the CANNOT DETERMINE list (lines with none). An unknown is NEVER summed as zero.
rules.verdict: PASS = two or more DISTRIBUTORS as defined above (distinct registered domains that each gave a price), and a unit price determinable at 1 / 100 / 1000 robots. CANNOT DETERMINE = fewer than two such distributors, or none. FAIL = the line as specified cannot be bought as specified from anyone read - either the part does not exist in the maker's own catalogue (B3: the 1 GB / 32 GB Radxa ZERO 3W SKU Pollen names is absent from Radxa's own table), or EVERY distributor that gave a price publishes a process rule this line's own artwork measurably violates (P1 and P2: minimum copper track 0.1500 mm measured over 879 and 383 segments in the committed .kicad_pcb, against a published 6 mil = 0.1524 mm line/space floor at both OSH Park and AdvancedPCB - short by 0.0024 mm). This second clause was added 2026-09-03 when the custom-PCB lines were priced for the first time; before that the definition had no bucket for 'priced by two, buildable by neither' and the page would have had to call such a line PASS. A FAIL line's readable money is reported OUTSIDE the headline subtotal, never inside it and never as zero.
rules.distributor: A DISTRIBUTOR is a REGISTERED DOMAIN that gave a price for OUR part on a page we read (offers[].confidence == 'read' AND offers[].tiers non-empty). Two corrections, both measured 2026-09-03. (1) Counting vendor NAME STRINGS let one shop entered under two spellings look like two distributors - DigiKey appears here as 'DigiKey', 'DigiKey (cut tape)' and 'DigiKey (cut tape / Digi-Reel)'. (2) Counting READ pages let a page that carried no price for our part count as a distributor: JLCPCB's home page prints 'From $2.00 / 5 pcs' and PCBWay's '$5.00 10 pcs 1-2 layer', both floors for somebody else's board. Such an offer is recorded with tiers: [] and counts toward nothing. tools/gen_sourcing.py enforces this in priced_domains(); the hole was proved by emptying tiers on one of B10's two read offers and watching the old code publish '2 distinct distributor(s) with a price read' anyway, and the fixed code exits 1 naming B10.
rules.custom_pcbs: The three custom boards P1 / P2 / P3 are quoted from THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN fab packages, not refused for want of them: electronics/robot-hat/out/fab/microduck_robot_hat-fab.zip (committed 077fe49), electronics/imu-to-dxl/... and electronics/banana-contact/... (committed e63dd4f). Each zip carries Gerbers (F/B.Cu, F/B.Mask, F/B.Silk, F/B.Paste), Edge.Cuts.GKO, PTH.drl + NPTH.drl, bom.csv, positions.csv and ORDER-NOTES.txt. Until 2026-09-03 these three lines read 'There is nothing to send a fab' and 'Board outline ... CANNOT DETERMINE' - a refusal the repository itself contradicted, and the reason the largest unknowns in the cost model stayed unpriced. Every board number in these lines is measured off the committed .kicad_pcb or Edge.Cuts.GKO, and each board's own DRC verdict is stated in the RFQ letter that goes out with it.
